thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 RED: Multiple serving pods in us-west-2 entering CrashLoopBackOff + CUDA OOMs, request error rate spike to 18% (5m). Paging: @alice (on-call)
alice: ack I'm on it, hitting the runbook now. can someone drop the recent deploy id?
bob: noticed a big spike in autoscaler activity around the same time — rapid scale down then immediate scale up. possible 'scale thrash' causing scheduling pressure.
carla: looking at cluster autoscaler logs. saw frequent node deletions from spot eviction + scale-down. will post snippets.
bob: reproducing pod logs, main error is `CUDA out of memory` inside runtime-worker. stack shows allocation failures during kv-cache warmup.
alice: tagging @dan for runtime input, and @erin for customer impact comms.
dan: I see repeated OOMs in the runtime container right after readiness probe passes. suspicious: pods get scheduled on newly-provisioned nodes with lower GPU drivers or stale CUDA version.
carla: from cloud console: multiple nodegroups scaled from 30 -> 8 -> 36 in ~10m. scale-down aggressiveness set to 0.5 min nodes, policy 'binpack' + aggressive TTL.
alice: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler 2) cordon suspicious nodes 3) route traffic away from the problematic model variant 4) fallback to smaller model if needed.
erin: customers seeing 5xx errors on text-generation endpoints. escalating to SEs — major accounts receiving errors.
sre-shift: I'll take autoscaler pause and cordon; @carla do you want the exact commands or want me to run?
carla: runbook gives `kubectl cordon` + `gcloud compute instances stop` but stop is heavy. better to `kubectl cordon` and taint nodes `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule`.
carla: paste: ```
# cordon nodes with label nodepool=ephemeral-spot
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=ephemeral-spot -o name); do
  kubectl cordon $n
  kubectl taint node $n ephemeral-thrash=true:NoSchedule || true
done
```
alice: doing it now. pausing cluster-autoscaler: ```kubectl scale deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --replicas=0``` — will hold capacity steady.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T14:03:21Z to serving-runtime failed on 3/12 pods: CrashLoopBackOff. Auto-rollback not triggered.
bob: while autoscaler was oscillating, some nodes landed on older GPU drivers (470.x) vs expected 525.x — mismatch causes drivers to allocate less effectively and triggers OOMs under the new kernel-mode scheduling paths.
dan: workaround: force scheduling to node pool with validated GPU AMI and prevent further spot nodes until we stabilize.
alice: routing change: switching traffic for model 'redwood-13b-v2' to dedicated pool 'dedicated-ml-1' (no spot) — applying weighted route 0.0 -> 1.0 over 30s.
alice: command: `roteroute set serving/redwood-13b-v2 --to dedicated-ml-1 --weight 100 --grace 30s`
erin: notifying affected customers: short message drafted — will send after we confirm routing taking effect. includes ETA: recovery within 20-30m.
carla: monitoring node churn metrics; node eviction rate down after cordon; autoscaler paused so no new scale events should occur.
sre-shift: observed pods being rescheduled now onto dedicated pool. success: 8/10 runtime pods online on dedicated nodes; 2 still CrashLoopBackOff.
bob: grabbing logs from one CrashLoop pod:
```
2026-03-15T14:18:02 runtime ERROR Failed to allocate 3.2GB for KV cache: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve/worker.py", line 412, in start
    cache.initialize(max_size_mb=768)
  File "/app/serve/cache.py", line 88, in initialize
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at ...
```
dan: that stack implies startup prewarming tries to allocate a bigger kv cache than node GPU memory allows. we can reduce `KV_CACHE_SIZE_MB` via configmap for the runtime; patch rollout to avoid full restarts.
alice: patching configmap to set KV_CACHE_SIZE_MB=512 (was 1024). will apply as a rolling restart of the replicaSet.
carla: be careful: rolling restarts while some pods OOM may cause additional churn. suggest we scale replicas down to 2, update, then scale back up to target.
sre-shift: good call. plan: scale serving-runtime to 2, apply configmap change, wait for stability, then scale back to desired replicas.
alice: executing: `kubectl scale deployment serving-runtime --replicas=2` -> succeeded.
alice: applying configmap patch and issuing restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime`.
dan: monitoring memory usage after patch. initial signs: new pods now initialize with smaller cache and reach ready. old CrashLoop pods continue to fail but should be replaced.
bob: also found GPU driver warnings in node syslogs on several nodes: `nvidia-smi repeated GPU hang detected` — those nodes we cordoned earlier.
carla: after scaling adjustments and routing to dedicated pool, request error rate reduced from 18% -> 4% in 12m.
erin: sent update to customers: brief note + we offered dedicated pool migration for impacted tenants; asking for any follow-ups.
alice: Post-incident tasks immediate: 1) confirm all model variants healthy 2) re-enable autoscaler with safer params 3) review nodegroup scaling policy and spot usage 4) retrospective on runtime prewarm configs.
bob: autoscaler reconfiguration suggestions: increase cooldown to 10m, min_nodes=10, disable aggressive binpack for spot pools, add scale-down-protected label for nodepools with model-specific GPUs.
carla: also propose autoscaler add a stabilization window to avoid thrash when node provisioning latency > 3m. we have metrics showing provisioning spikes.
dan: runtime change: default KV cache should be adaptive to GPU memory detected at startup; patch in PR to follow.
alice: can someone capture exact customer impact list and total error counts? @erin
erin: pulling from metrics now. impacted tenants: acme-inc (30% of their requests), beta-apps (10%), several smaller customers. error events ~ 24k 5xx in 15m window.
sre-shift: documenting time line for postmortem: incident start 2062404827, mitigation: cordon+pause autoscaler at +6m, route to dedicated pool at +9m, configmap patch completed +18m, error rate mostly recovered +30m.
alice: assigning follow-ups: @carla autoscaler policy changes + PR; @dan runtime adaptive cache PR; @bob driver verification & imaging for spot nodes; @erin customer comms follow-up + SLA impact calc.
deploy-bot: note: the deployment that coincided with the start was `serving-runtime:v2026-03-15-946`. it passed e2e in canary but exposed kv cache default that assumes 16GB GPUs.
alice: action: create postmortem doc and link to incident channel. minimal blameless timeline + next steps. I will start draft.
erin: customers acknowledged and appreciated the pace; offering credit for impacted period. I'll coordinate with sales.
carla: once postmortem is up, propose a test matrix to validate new autoscaler params in staging with simulated provisioning delay and spot evictions.
alice: final check — all runtime pods ready? status shows 12/12 healthy across dedicated and stable nodepools. error rate ~1.1% now.
alice: closing the live pager for now. will keep channel open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident CLOSED (auto): severity reduced to SEV2, routed to postmortem workflow.
summary: Autoscaler oscillation + mixed GPU drivers caused CUDA OOMs and CrashLoopBackOffs; paused autoscaler, cordoned nodes, routed traffic to dedicated pool, reduced KV cache, scaled down/up; recovered within ~30m; follow-ups assigned.
